mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI annualized growth > 2% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous two months signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased corporate costs and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.5pp does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous two months signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase > 5% does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease > 1% does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) growth is below 1% annualized over the previous two months, it signals a disinflationary environment with high real interest rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: disinflationary environment with high real rates
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL < 1% annualized growth does not correlate with negative returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month signals strong labor demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of instances with PAYEMS increase > 200,000, or PAYEMS increase > 200,000 does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 5% annually and GDP (GDPC1) grows by less than 2% annually over the previous quarter, it signals a demand-driven economy with potential overheating, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS annual growth > 5% and GDPC1 annual growth < 2%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of RSAFS > 5% and GDPC1 < 2% annual growth does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25 percentage points over the previous month signals a loosening monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease > 0.25pp does not correlate with positive returns (Pearson correlation p > 0.05).
